features.title: One tab semantics provider for Workbench and standalone fallback
features.summary: The declared main-tabs/workbench-tabs public module re-exports the canonical workbench/tabs page-global snapshot/subscribe/actions bridge. Workbench adopts the existing actor's current set, computed status/unread/preview/pin/title/availability and scoped targets without opening tabs again. User actions drive that same actor; workbench aside moves preserve the actor tab and only accepted native independent-pane moves close the source. The owned stack always uses Workbench pane chrome, with no native-layout opt-out; its conversation actor stays enabled despite a legacy disabled standalone-strip preference. Normal sidebar opens keep separate Session-bound conversation tabs without a disposable preview, while panel opening modes remain configurable. The fullheight right pane retains its tabs while collapsed. The native strip and mount observer are removed without hiding shell.main; their original route remains only for absent-Workbench deployments. Semantic Start shows the same Choose a view / Search views chooser as a group's New tab, including one Settings Shell: Settings hub and qualified plugin views, but no separate Rich Composer/current-conversation clone. The thread list explicitly opens or focuses fixed Session-bound chat-and-editor tabs, including same-native-current reopen after closing all tabs; standalone fallback Start suggestions remain unchanged.

Selecting a conversation from another project must not select that project's saved scene or remove an unrelated chooser; the Workbench scene anchor and native Host project metadata have separate meanings.

features.title: Browser-like tabs above the main view
features.summary: Every thread or global panel shown in the main view opens or focuses a tab above it. The strip looks like DSH's own right-panel tabs (28px pills and hairline separators), and one profile setting places its close button to the left or right of the title on both the strip and Workbench headers. Tabs close with × or a middle click, reorder by drag, pin to the start, close others or to the right from their context menu, scroll or list in a dropdown when they overflow, and show working, needs-you and unread dots on thread tabs. A thread tab's menu opens that thread in the right side panel — through the cancelable `dshfiles:open-thread-aside` event `@dshfiles/thread-sidebar` answers, with the strip saying the panel is unavailable when no plugin takes it — and dragging a thread tab onto the open side panel moves it there instead: the right column highlights under the pointer, and dropping closes the main tab once the aside took the thread. The aside tab's own menu moves it back through `dshfiles:open-thread`. Thread tabs also copy their ID or a clean deep link, their menu's Edit title edits the title in place, and their menu can insert that thread into the active composer as a native @mention; Copy groups copy actions, and Change status groups status actions such as settling through thread-sidebar. A thread tab dragged onto a composer mentions it there instead of reordering: the tab drag carries the thread-mention type rather than plain text, so the editor never receives a stray title. Panel openings and standalone conversation tabs use a VS Code-style preview by default; Workbench conversations are kept in separate Session-bound tabs after normal sidebar clicks, independently of the legacy standalone-strip toggle. A panel plugin that shows different subjects can keep one tab per subject: it asks for a tab with `dshfiles:open-panel-tab` (`{ panelId, scope, title? }`), the strip announces `dshfiles:panel-scope` before navigating so the plugin swaps what it shows, and a live `dshfiles:panel-tab-title` renames the tab. Scope and title are saved with the tab, so a reload restores the same tab on the same subject.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; enable the standalone compatibility strip. Workbench always enables the shared semantic owner, including when an old profile saved false; saved settings are not overwritten.
Places tab close buttons on the selected side of titles in the main strip and Workbench headers.
Integer 2–50; past it the least recently used unpinned tab closes.
Panels and standalone conversations use preview, new or replace. Workbench conversations are kept independently even with a saved preview or replace mode; panel previews are unchanged.

failureModes: A tab whose panel plugin is gone stays dimmed until the panel registers again; picking it does nothing.
A navigation the Host never finishes stops being awaited after two seconds.
Tabs of deleted threads are dropped.

Open in side panel leaves the thread alone and the strip announces that the side panel is unavailable there when no plugin offers an aside, and a request with no thread on screen is declined the same way.

Dragging a panel tab over the right column asks its plugin through the cancelable `dshfiles:move-panel-aside` event. A panel whose plugin offers no side-panel view keeps its tab and the strip says so; a panel tab is only moved when its owner cancels the request.
A thread dropped where the aside owner declined the request keeps its main tab and announces the unavailable side panel; dragging where the right sidebar is not mounted highlights nothing.

If DSH stops rendering the main slot outlet (`[data-slot="main"]`) the strip stays hidden, tabs keep following the main view, and the console warns once at startup; if the strip lands anywhere but directly above the main panel, the console warns too.
A thread tab dropped outside the active composer leaves the strip alone; a drop on the composer inserts a mention chip and never the tab title as plain text.
A same-origin thread link whose thread the strip cannot open (unlisted, archived, or main-tabs switched off) keeps the link's own navigation instead of opening a tab.

features.title: Open a new tab with suggestions of what to show
features.summary: In the standalone fallback (unchanged), "+" at the end of the strip (or Mod+T on Desktop, Mod+Alt+T on the Web) opens a Start tab with a focused command-palette search. Typing filters New thread, the five most recent threads (running ones first), main panels and Settings by title or description; Arrow keys and Enter pick a result. The picked thread or panel takes the Start tab's place, while New thread and Settings close it.

features.title: Jump between tabs from the keyboard
features.summary: Close active tab closes the active tab without archiving its thread; it ships without a default because DSH's own page.close owns Mod+W, and is bound in Settings › Shortcuts. Mod+1…8 jump to a tab and Mod+9 to the last one, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle (Desktop); the browser keeps those keys, so the Web defaults are Mod+Alt+1…9 and Mod+Alt+] / [. All are rebindable in Settings › Shortcuts. Arrow keys, Enter and Delete work inside the focused strip. Mod+T (Web: Mod+Alt+T) opens a new tab.
failureModes: A default another command already owns leaves that tab command listed but unbound.

features.title: Keep tabs across reloads, per project or globally
features.summary: The tab set, order, pins, preview flag, active tab, and each scoped panel tab's scope and title survive a reload. Native fallback follows per-project sets unless the persistence setting shares one set; Workbench holds the adopted window scene while selecting conversations across projects, without merging dormant sets or rewriting preferences. An explicit persistence change can still select another scene. A reload that lands on the New thread screen reopens the saved active tab.

configuration.constraints: Native project mode follows each project's saved set; global shares one. Workbench holds the adopted window scene during subject navigation; an explicit preference change can still select another scene.
